A day for each feast

Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Candlemas Celebration at Home

Celebrate Candlemas by honoring the tradition of blessing candles, enjoying winter light, and sharing festive foods that reflect both European and Mexican customs.

  1. Morning

    Prepare and Bless Candles

    Begin the day by gathering candles to be blessed. Light them to symbolize hope and protection for the coming year, following the ancient tradition of Candlemas.

  2. Late Morning

    Make Traditional Crepes

    Prepare crepes beurre sucre and crepes jambon-fromage to enjoy a classic French Candlemas meal, symbolizing the sun and the return of longer days.

    Recipes: Crepes Beurre Sucre · Crepes Jambon-Fromage

  3. Noon

    Light a Candlelit Procession at Home

    Hold a small procession around your home or garden with the blessed candles, illuminating the winter afternoon and embracing the festival’s focus on light.

  4. Afternoon

    Prepare Mexican Tamales and Drinks

    Cook tamales oaxaquenos and tamales de dulce, and prepare atole de canela and champurrado espumoso, honoring Mexican Candlemas traditions after the blessing of candles.

    Recipes: Tamales Oaxaqueños · Tamales De Dulce · Atole De Canela · Champurrado Espumoso

  5. Late Afternoon

    Enjoy a Light Salad and Cider

    Serve salade de mache alongside boles de cidre brut to balance the rich tamales and crepes with fresh greens and crisp cider.

    Recipes: Salade de Mâche · Boles De Cidre Brut

  6. Evening

    Share Pan de Candelaria

    Conclude the day by sharing pan de candelaria, a sweet bread symbolizing the feast and community, perfect for reflecting on the day’s blessings.

    Recipes: Pan De Candelaria

End your Candlemas celebration by keeping your blessed candles lit a little longer, welcoming light and warmth into the winter season.
